title: Please Let the Internet Die
gist: Miles Klee uses John West's book The Internet Will Die, and So Will You to argue the current web is decaying under AI slop, bots and engagement incentives, while its fragility and cycles of rebirth leave room for a more organic web.

insights.claim: One cybersecurity firm concluded this spring that agents already outnumber human users online, with agent traffic surging 8,000 percent through 2025.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Bot-dominated traffic undermines engagement metrics and ad value; supports Dead Internet Theory.
insights.quote: agents already outnumber human users, their traffic surging by 8,000 percent through 2025

insights.claim: Generative AI has become a turbocharged slop engine filling feeds and comment sections with useless content, eroding consumer appeal, while data centers that power it grow unpopular and politically radioactive.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Consumer sentiment and political backlash are rising risks to the AI build-out narrative.
insights.locator: Generative AI, briefly considered an amusing novelty

insights.claim: Meta and Google have settled massive consumer lawsuits over privacy violations and mental-health harms from addictive platform design, and schools and countries are restricting phones and under-16 social media.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Regulatory and litigation pressure on attention-based business models is rising.

insights.claim: Oxford University Press named rage bait the word of the year in December after use tripled, reflecting monetized accounts using generative AI to automate hostile engagement.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Engagement-farming incentives persist and are being automated.
insights.locator: To be online, many now admit

insights.claim: Billionaire oligarchs have opened the floodgates to inauthentic activity and hate speech by rolling back moderation.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Moderation rollback raises brand-safety risk for advertisers.
insights.locator: To be online, many now admit

insights.claim: The internet is fragile and impermanent: a 2001 Baltimore tunnel train derailment took out a major fiber bundle and slowed internet nationwide, and West says the web is a rounding error of human experience.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Infrastructure concentration is a persistent fragility.
insights.quote: a vanishing fraction, a rounding error, of the human experience
insights.locator: If the internet is much smaller

insights.claim: An analysis found 25 percent of links in New York Times articles from 1996 to mid-2019 were inaccessible, a 2016 study found three of four scholarly citations had drifted, and Pew found over half of Wikipedia entries contain a dead reference link.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Link rot erodes the web's value as a durable record, raising the premium on archives and verified sources.

insights.claim: West argues the internet's sense of permanence is false and that platforms like Vine can vanish instantly, as TikTok users' farewell videos ahead of an expected US ban in January 2025 illustrated.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Platform concentration risk applies to creators and advertisers.
insights.quote: “‘Forever’ is such a strong word, and it's the wrong word,”

insights.claim: West argues that leaving the mainstream platforms may be the last lever available to the public, freeing people to explore dormant corners where meaning exists without financial motivation.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Attention exits could erode usage of ad-driven platforms, but there is no evidence of scale.

insights.claim: West frames internet decay as compost, rot harnessed for a purpose, and the article suggests the organic web could mount a renaissance if the present tech empire falls, though the author doubts enough people will act.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Speculative; signals appetite for alternatives to platform incumbents.
insights.quote: Compost is just rot harnessed for a purpose

insights.claim: Absent a catastrophic outage the internet as it exists won't perish soon, and there is no reason to assume the present tech empire will rule the century to come.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Long-run incumbent durability is not guaranteed in the author's view.
